dedupe_keys.name: gnss realistic planning web processing service university of genoa and university of trento 2009

description: This paper describes a web processing service for realistic GNSS survey planning. Using a digital surface model to build the obstruction plot and the satellite almanac to evaluate visibility, a GIS procedure automatically computes, for a whole area, the minimum number of visible satellites and the PDOP index in every pixel, replacing hand-drawn polar obstruction diagrams. The procedure was developed in the open source GIS GRASS and offered as an OGC Web Processing Service through PyWPS, with a simple WebGIS interface for non-specialists. Users choose the constellation (GPS or GPS and GLONASS), cut-off elevation angle, day, hour and time window; the almanac is downloaded daily from Trimble, and outputs are five ASCII grid maps plus WebGIS layers. Some UNAVCO TEQC features help site new permanent stations. Producer: Bianca Federici, Davide Giacomelli, Domenico Sguerso, Alfonso Vitti and Paolo Zatelli, ISPRS workshop paper, 2009 to 2010. Coverage: any area with a digital surface model. Access: paper on the ISPRS archive; the service address and code are not given in the paper, so availability today is unverified. Licence and cost: paper free; the implementation is built on free and open source components but no release licence was seen. Caveats: GPS and GLONASS only, almanac source may have changed since 2010. Simulation uses: pixel-level satellite count and PDOP maps support planning of positioning networks and coverage under obstruction. Related records: none linked.
